subject: English Language Arts

questions.text: Use the word bank (knit, limb, reigns, wring, rhythm, wrong, gnaw, knight, comb) to complete this sentence: "A king ___ best from his throne in the castle."
Use the word bank to complete this sentence: "To make a wet sponge dry, you need to ___ it out."
Use the word bank to complete this sentence: "If you listen to lively music, you can't help but dance to the ___."
Use the word bank to complete this sentence: "To fight a pesky dragon, call a strong and fearless ___."
The page title lists the silent letter pairs kn, wr, gn, mb, and rh. Which pair of words in the word bank both contain the letters mb?
On the word web for the word torch, which phrase is printed in an outer oval?
On the word web, which vocabulary word is connected to the word artist?
On the word web, which vocabulary word is connected to the phrase strong feeling?
On the word webs, the word monument is connected to which word?
On the word web printed on page 70, which word is connected to ferry?
According to the lesson on this page, the central idea is ___.

options.A: the first sentence of a text
options.B: the longest paragraph in a text
options.C: what a text is mostly about
options.D: the title printed at the top of a text

questions.text: According to the page, which clues help readers identify the central idea?

options.C: the author's name and the title

questions.text: According to the page, what provides evidence to support the central idea?

options.C: the number of paragraphs in the text

questions.text: A text has the heading "How Ferries Carry People." According to the page, this heading is a clue that helps a reader ___.
According to the page, a prefix is ___.

options.A: a picture that shows a word's meaning
options.B: a word part added to the end of a base word
options.C: a word part added to the beginning of a base word that changes the meaning of the word
options.D: a word that rhymes with a base word

questions.text: Add the prefix im- to a word from the word bank (possible, patient, polite, balance, movable) to complete the story: "Amos tried to hurry, but it was ___ to get his chores done any faster."
Add the prefix im- to a word from the word bank to complete the story: "There is an ___ of work here. You finished cleaning your half of the basement first."
Add the prefix im- to a word from the word bank to complete the story: Amos says the heavy boxes are ___, so they are hard to move.
Add the prefix im- to a word from the word bank to complete the story: Zeke says, "That was ___ of me. I'll help you move the boxes."
Word bank: possible, patient, polite, balance, movable. The story calls the heavy boxes immovable. Adding the prefix im- to which word bank word forms the word immovable?
According to the page, what is an author's purpose?

options.A: the reason an author writes a text
options.B: the number of pages in a text
options.C: the place where a text takes place

questions.text: According to the page, why do authors write?

options.B: to share an idea or a message
options.C: to give directions to a place
options.D: to sell copies of a book

questions.text: A test asks, "What is the author's purpose for writing this selection?" What is the test asking you to find?

options.A: the number of characters in the selection
options.C: the reason the author wrote the text

questions.text: The word bank includes the word knuckle. Which clue does knuckle answer?
Which word from the word bank means "protective gear worn by a skateboarder"?
The page title lists the silent-letter pair wr. Which word from the word bank begins with wr?
Which word from the word bank contains the silent-letter pair gn?
The page title lists the silent-letter pair rh. Which word from the word bank begins with rh?
According to the page, what are literary elements?

options.A: the pieces that make up a story

questions.text: According to the page, characters are -

options.A: the events that happen in a story
options.B: the people and animals in a story
options.D: where and when a story takes place

questions.text: According to the page, the setting of a story is -

options.A: the events that happen in the story
options.C: where and when the story takes place
options.D: the people and animals in the story

questions.text: In a story, a boy loses his kite, searches the park, and finds it in a tree. Which literary element is this?
Which question would help you identify the setting of a story?

options.A: Where and when does the story take place?
options.B: What events happen in the story?
options.D: Who are the people and animals in the story?

questions.text: Which word from the word bank means "a question word"?
Which word from the word bank means "season after winter"?
Which word from the word bank begins with the digraph ph?
Which word from the word bank ends with the digraph tch?
Which word from the word bank means "money"?
The page defines a prefix as a word part that does what?

options.A: It is added to the end of a base word and changes the word's meaning.
options.C: It is added to the beginning of a base word and changes the word's meaning.
options.D: It replaces the base word with a synonym.

questions.text: Using the word bank (peril, complete, migrate, accurate, print, active), which word completes sentence 1: 'My pet mouse is ______ lately and won't use her running wheel.'?
Using the word bank (peril, complete, migrate, accurate, print, active), which word completes sentence 3: 'Many people ______ to this country from other places.'?
Which word correctly adds the prefix in- to the base word accurate to complete sentence 4: 'Be careful to get the facts right so you don't say something ______ during the debate.'?
Which word completes sentence 5: 'I don't know how to end the story I'm writing, so it is still ______.'?
Which word completes sentence 6: 'If you want to stay safe, don't ______ yourself by going skydiving!'?
The page heading says the prefix in- means 'not.' If visible means 'able to be seen,' which word most likely means 'not able to be seen'?
According to the page, the plot of a story includes which two parts?
Which group correctly lists the main literary elements named on the page?

options.C: characters; setting; plot; and the events

questions.text: A student says the main literary elements are only the characters and the setting. Based on the page's definition, what is missing from that list?

options.B: the narrator and the stage directions
options.D: the plot, which includes the conflict and resolution, and the events

questions.text: How does the page define figurative language?

options.A: words or expressions that mean something different from their dictionary definitions
options.B: the exact dictionary meaning of a word
options.C: the order of events in a story
options.D: words that are spelled exactly as they sound

questions.text: Which three examples of figurative language does the page list?
Question 2 on the page asks what details make a scene a good example of 'hyperbole, or ______.' Which word completes the question?
What does the instruction at the top of the page tell you to do with the words you learn from reading?

options.B: Look each word up in a glossary.
options.C: Use them only on spelling tests.
options.D: Use them as you talk and write.
